description: Add ECS concurrency guard to silver catchup CLI so EventBridge can fire frequently without overlapping runs — the guard must be the very first check (before any S3 calls) to minimize cost of skipped invocations
steps: [DONE] Add --skip-if-concurrent flag to the `silver catchup` command in silver.py, following the same pattern used by Bronze backfill catchup (see cli/main.py backfill_catchup --skip-if-concurrent)

[DONE] Derive an entity-scoped concurrency filter string from --platform and --entity args (e.g. 'silver-polymarket-trades') so that different entity types CAN run concurrently but the SAME entity type CANNOT overlap — this is critical because EventBridge will fire every 10 min and a slow trades run must not block markets/events

[DONE] Place the should_skip_concurrent() call as the ABSOLUTE FIRST operation in _run_catchup() — before state store load, manifest discovery, markets reference load, or any S3/Glue calls — a skipped run should cost only the ECS cold start (~30s) plus one ECS API call, nothing more
[DONE] When a concurrent run is detected, log a structured info message (not warning — this is normal expected behavior under near-continuous scheduling) and exit with code 0
[DONE] Add --skip-if-concurrent flag to the `silver maintain` command as well — daily compaction and weekly full maintenance should not overlap with each other or with a long-running catchup

[DONE] Add unit tests: verify should_skip_concurrent is called with the correct entity-scoped filter string, verify clean exit on concurrent detection, verify normal proceed when no concurrent run, verify maintain also respects the flag
[DONE] Run mypy and ruff on all changed files

description: Ensure silver catchup exits as fast as possible when there is nothing to process — under near-continuous scheduling the majority of invocations will be no-ops and must be extremely cheap
steps: [DONE] Audit the _run_catchup() hot path for no-op runs (committed in 3d03e41): path is state_store.load() → discover_manifests() → filter already-processed → early-return if empty. Markets reference and Glue catalog are NOT loaded on the no-op path. Architecture is correct — empirical timing verification deferred to deployment_and_validation category

[DONE] Verified markets reference loading is ONLY triggered after the 'All manifests already processed' early-return check — confirmed in silver.py lines 629-650 (committed in 3d03e41). The most expensive startup operation is completely skipped on no-op runs

[DONE] Add structured logging for the no-op exit path with timing: emit a 'silver_catchup_noop' structured log event with duration_seconds at the 'Silver is up to date' return point, so CloudWatch can track how fast no-op exits are and alert if they degrade

Consider adding a lightweight pre-check: before full manifest discovery, check if any new Bronze prefixes exist since the last known processed run_id using a single S3 list_objects_v2 with start_after — this could skip the full discover_manifests() call entirely on no-op runs (implement only if manifest discovery takes >5s in the no-new-data case, measured during deployment_and_validation)

description: Create CloudFormation template for Silver EventBridge Scheduler schedules — near-continuous processing with per-entity concurrency guards, following the exact conventions of eventbridge-schedules.yaml and eventbridge-gold-schedules.yaml
steps: Create infrastructure/eventbridge-silver-schedules.yaml with the same Parameters block pattern as eventbridge-schedules.yaml: Environment, ECSClusterArn, TaskDefinitionArn, SubnetIds, SecurityGroupIds, ScheduleTimezone, ScheduleState, plus per-cadence schedule expression parameters

Create IAM role: prediction-data-silver-scheduler-{Environment} — same trust policy (scheduler.amazonaws.com) and permissions (ecs:RunTask scoped to TaskDefinitionArn, iam:PassRole scoped to ecs-tasks service) as Bronze/Gold scheduler roles
Create schedule group: prediction-data-silver-{Environment} with Project=prediction-data, Layer=silver, Environment tags

Add schedule: silver-polymarket-trades-{env}, rate(10 minutes), command=['silver', 'catchup', '--platform', 'polymarket', '--entity', 'trades', '--skip-if-concurrent'] — highest frequency because Bronze order_filled ingests every 5 min; data appears in Silver within ~15 min of on-chain event

Add schedule: silver-polymarket-markets-{env}, rate(30 minutes), command=['silver', 'catchup', '--platform', 'polymarket', '--entity', 'markets', '--skip-if-concurrent'] — Bronze markets ingests hourly; 30-min Silver cadence catches updates within one Bronze cycle
Add schedule: silver-polymarket-events-{env}, rate(30 minutes), command=['silver', 'catchup', '--platform', 'polymarket', '--entity', 'events', '--skip-if-concurrent'] — same rationale as markets
Add schedule: silver-kalshi-trades-{env}, rate(10 minutes), State=DISABLED — scaffold for when Kalshi data pipeline is activated
Add schedule: silver-kalshi-markets-{env}, rate(30 minutes), State=DISABLED
Add schedule: silver-kalshi-events-{env}, rate(30 minutes), State=DISABLED

Add schedule: silver-maintain-compact-{env}, cron(0 4 * * ? *) daily at 04:00 UTC, command=['silver', 'maintain', '--op', 'compact', '--skip-if-concurrent'] — runs during overnight low-activity window after catchup processing settles

Add schedule: silver-maintain-full-{env}, cron(0 4 ? * SUN *) weekly Sunday 04:00 UTC, command=['silver', 'maintain', '--skip-if-concurrent'] — compact + expire + orphans; concurrency guard prevents overlap with daily compact if Sunday job runs late

Set RetryPolicy for catchup schedules: MaximumRetryAttempts=1, MaximumEventAgeInSeconds=300 — short retry window because the next scheduled invocation (10 or 30 min later) will pick up where this one failed; long retries waste money
Set RetryPolicy for maintenance schedules: MaximumRetryAttempts=2, MaximumEventAgeInSeconds=1800 — maintenance runs daily/weekly so retries are more valuable
Set FlexibleTimeWindow Mode=OFF for ALL schedules — exact timing; concurrency guard handles overlap, no need for jitter

Add parameterized schedule expressions (SilverTradesScheduleExpression, SilverCatalogScheduleExpression, etc.) so cadence can be tuned without modifying the template — default to rate(10 minutes) and rate(30 minutes) respectively
Add Outputs: SilverScheduleGroupArn, SilverScheduleGroupName, SilverSchedulerRoleArn, DeploymentCommand (with example aws cloudformation deploy command)

description: Add CloudWatch metric filters, alarms, and dashboard panels for Silver schedules — must distinguish between actual processing, no-op exits, and concurrency skips to verify the near-continuous model is healthy
steps: Add metric filter: SilverProcessingSuccess — pattern 'All manifests processed successfully' in /ecs/prediction-data-{env} log group, filtered to silver commands

Add metric filter: SilverNoOp — pattern 'Silver is up to date' — tracks frequency of no-work invocations (expected to be >50% of runs under near-continuous scheduling; validates that the guard+state model is working efficiently)

Add metric filter: SilverConcurrencySkip — pattern 'Concurrent task detected' filtered to silver commands — tracks how often the concurrency guard fires; a sustained high rate indicates processing duration exceeds the schedule interval and cadence should be reduced
Add metric filter: SilverProcessingFailure — pattern 'FAILED' in Silver catchup output

Add alarm: SilverTradesMissingRuns — if zero (SilverProcessingSuccess + SilverNoOp) for polymarket trades in 1 hour, alert; at 10-min cadence we expect ~6 runs/hour, zero means the schedule or ECS is broken
Add alarm: SilverProcessingErrors — if SilverProcessingFailure count > 3 in 30 minutes, alert; occasional failures are expected (transient S3 errors) but sustained failures need investigation
Add Silver panels to the existing CloudWatch dashboard: Silver runs by entity type (success vs noop vs skip vs failure), concurrency skip rate over time, processing duration histogram

description: Update infrastructure documentation, operational runbooks, and CLAUDE.md for the new Silver automation layer
steps: Add eventbridge-silver-schedules.yaml to infrastructure/README.md templates table with stack name prediction-data-silver-schedules and description

Add deployment command to README.md deployment order section as step 5c (between Gold schedules at 5b and CloudWatch monitoring at 6), including full aws cloudformation deploy example with parameter-overrides
Add Silver schedule group to README.md Resource Summary table: prediction-data-silver-{env}
Add Silver schedules to README.md rollback procedures (delete between Gold schedules and ECS cluster in reverse order)

Update OPERATIONS.md Silver Processing section: replace the example cron expressions with references to the deployed EventBridge schedules, update the production cadence description to reflect near-continuous model (every 10 min for trades, every 30 min for catalog), update the 'Future: Near-Real-Time Silver' section to note this is now implemented
Update CLAUDE.md Silver CLI section to document the --skip-if-concurrent flag on silver catchup and silver maintain, and document the silver catchup command

description: Deploy the Silver EventBridge stack to production and validate end-to-end that near-continuous processing works correctly — verify efficiency, concurrency safety, and cost profile over a 24-hour observation window
steps: Deploy eventbridge-silver-schedules.yaml via aws cloudformation deploy with Polymarket schedules ENABLED and Kalshi schedules DISABLED
Verify all 11 schedules appear in EventBridge Scheduler console under the prediction-data-silver-{env} group (6 Polymarket ENABLED, 3 Kalshi DISABLED, 2 maintenance ENABLED)
Validate first triggered run: wait for EventBridge to fire the polymarket-trades schedule, verify ECS task starts, silver catchup processes any pending manifests, and state store is updated

Validate concurrency guard: while a silver-polymarket-trades run is active, manually invoke a second ECS task with the same command via aws ecs run-task; verify it exits within 30 seconds with 'Concurrent task detected' and exit code 0

Validate no-op efficiency: wait for a run cycle where no new Bronze manifests exist, verify the ECS task exits within 60 seconds with 'Silver is up to date' — this is the critical efficiency test since most runs will be no-ops
Validate maintenance: manually invoke silver maintain --op compact --dry-run via ECS to verify task permissions and Glue catalog access are correct

Monitor CloudWatch for 24 hours: verify SilverProcessingSuccess > 0 for each Polymarket entity type, SilverNoOp count is reasonable (>50% of total runs), SilverConcurrencySkip rate is low (<10% of total runs), zero sustained SilverProcessingFailure

Review ECS cost for the 24-hour window: calculate total Fargate vCPU-hours and GB-hours consumed by Silver schedules, verify it is under $2/day (target: ~$0.50-1.00/day for no-op-dominated workload at 0.25 vCPU/512MB per task)
